function: Learned joint receive beamforming and fluid-antenna positioning that maximizes the number of clients selected for over-the-air FL aggregation under an MSE limit (pp. 4-5).
system: 100 single-antenna users (Table I lists 10), AP with 5 fluid antennas on a 1-D line of 8 wavelengths, Rician fading, no RIS, no frequency stated (pp. 2-3, 6).
method: Deep reinforcement learning (LSTM-DDPG actor-critic, LSTM in actor, replay buffer, Adam, 6000 episodes) at the AP; the aggregated FL model uses FedAvg over the air (pp. 2, 5-6).
data_channel: Custom simulated Rician fading channel (Kr=8) with users at random distances 20-100 m and AoAs in [-pi/2, pi/2]; MNIST only for the FL task (pp. 3, 6, 8).
test_conditions: 6000 training episodes on simulated Rician channels (N=5, Kr=8); extra runs with Kr=6 and other K, N, tau; reuse of a trained agent is not stated (pp. 6-7).
baselines: Non-learned: random beamforming, full-participation and ideal-FL benchmarks; learned: DDPG, SAC; FPA = own LSTM-DDPG with fixed antennas (pp. 6-8).
metrics: Number of selected clients, average DRL reward per episode, MNIST test accuracy (Fig. 6, Table II), FLOPs of the algorithm; aggregation MSE as constraint (pp. 6-8).
complexity: Action selection O(L^2), training O(HL^2) with L neurons per layer and batch H; FLOPs plotted against H and N (Fig. 1); +8.32% for N=10 to 20 (pp. 5-6).
q1_support: p. 3: "we adopt the rician fading model"; Table I (p. 6) lists the channel gain as Rician. It is a custom simulator with random distances and angles (p. 6); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 7: "We conducted additional simulations with Kr = 6 and observed that the proposed algorithm maintains highly robust performance". The paper does not say that an agent trained at Kr = 8 was tested at Kr = 6, nor that the sweeps over K, N and tau (Figs. 3-5) reuse a trained agent.
q3_support: p. 6: "we assess the LSTM-DDPG algorithm against the SAC algorithm [26], [39], [40] and the standard DDPG algorithm [29] based on average rewards"; p. 7: "the proposed FA method consistently outperforms both FPA and the random algorithm". Borderline, see notes.
q4_support: p. 6: "Fig. 1 presents the number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) required by the proposed algorithm"; Section V-A (pp. 5-6) gives O(HL^2) for training and O(L^2) for action selection, and "an 8.32% increase in computational load" from N = 10 to 20.
q5_support: p. 8: "collaborative training of image classification models using the MNIST dataset" is a public dataset of the learning task only, which does not count; channels are simulated (p. 3, Eq. 5) and no link to code or data is given.
notes: Area 7 because the problem is the over-the-air aggregation of FL (aggregation MSE and number of admitted clients); the agent outputs beamformer and antenna positions and client selection follows from a threshold on the beamformed channel gain (Eq. 22, p. 4), so the learned decision is physical layer. Fluid antennas at the AP are not a RIS. The AP has 5 antennas, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. Table I (p. 6) says K=10 users, the text (p. 6) says 100. Q3 is borderline: DDPG and SAC are compared only through the training reward (Fig. 2, p. 7), which equals the number of selected users; the FPA curve is the proposed LSTM-DDPG with fixed antennas (a variant) and Random is the paper's own heuristic; the reviewer should confirm. Tables I-II and Figs. 1-6 were read from the page images (pp. 6-8).
